item.title: Attempted stabbing attack at Damascus Gate in Jerusalem, terrorist neutralized
item.description:
A terrorist attempted to stab a police officer at Damascus Gate in Jerusalem's Old City.
Police officers opened fire at the suspect and neutralized him. No injuries among police officers have been reported.

item.title: 78-year-old moderately injured in apartment building fire in Rishon LeZion
item.description:
A 78-year-old man was moderately injured and another person sustained minor injuries in a fire at a residential building in Rishon LeZion.
Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics provided medical treatment and evacuated both victims to Shamir-Assaf Harofeh Hospital with signs of smoke inhalation.

item.title: US House passes bill cutting aid to colleges that participate in BDS boycotts
item.description: US House of Representatives passes bill that could cut federal student aid to colleges engaging in commercial or academic boycotts of Israel.

item.title: Electric scooter rider injured in Tel Aviv, condition serious
item.description:
An approximately 18-year-old electric scooter rider was seriously injured after falling while riding in Tel Aviv.
Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics evacuated him to Ichilov Hospital in the city.

item.title: More than 50,000 attend Selichot prayer service at Western Wall
item.description: More than 50,000 people attend central Selichot prayer service at the Western Wall. Due to the large crowds, the service was broadcast on giant screens along the Old City walls.

item.title: IDF strikes following fire targeting its forces in northern Gaza
item.description:
A short while ago, fire was identified toward IDF troops operating east of the Yellow Line in the northern Gaza Strip. No IDF injuries were reported.
The IDF Spokesperson's Unit said, "The IDF struck in the area. This constitutes a blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement in the Gaza Strip. The IDF views with severity the attempts by the terrorist organizations in the Gaza Strip to advance and execute attacks against IDF troops operating in the area."

item.title: Trump hosts rabbis and Hasidic leaders at White House, including Satmar’s two rebbes
item.description:
US President Donald Trump hosted prominent American rabbis and Hasidic leaders at the White House, including the two rebbes of the Satmar Hasidic community, brothers who lead two separate Satmar congregations.
Satmar is one of the largest Hasidic groups in New York, with tens of thousands of followers. Both rebbes are part of the leadership of the anti-Zionist Hasidic movement.

item.title: Vance: US won’t talk to Iran until it stops attacking commercial ships
item.description: Vice President JD Vance says the US will not resume talks with Iran until Tehran stops attacking commercial ships: “Stop acting like crazy people."

item.title: Report in Iran: Missiles launched toward Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iranian media reported that missiles were launched toward the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Six arrested over suspected attack on business owner in Jerusalem’s Har Homa neighborhood
item.description:
Jerusalem District Police officers arrested six suspects who allegedly arrived at a business in the Har Homa neighborhood amid a criminal dispute and attacked the business owner.
One person was lightly injured and taken to a hospital for medical treatment. The suspects were taken in for questioning.

item.title: Supreme Court unanimously strikes down law freezing arrests of haredi draft evaders
item.description: Nine-judge panel strikes down the amendment freezing enforcement proceedings against haredi men subject to military service. Eight rule it was also unconstitutional.

item.title: Ben Gvir and Tally Gotliv to hold joint statement on Friday
item.description: Otzma Yehudit chairman and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir and MK Tally Gotliv will hold a joint statement to the media on Friday at 12:00 p.m. at Beit Zioni America in Tel Aviv.

item.title: Gafni: Finance officials threatened to freeze yeshiva funds
item.description: Degel HaTorah chairman MK Moshe Gafni claims Finance Ministry officials threatened yeshiva funding if he continued backing regional councils and Israeli agriculture.

item.description: New survey shows Likud holds commanding lead with 31 seats as 'Together' gains ground and Ofer Winter’s 'Amcha Yisrael' falls to just 2.7%.
